title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-ready slug

criteria.text: Giving slugify a title returns a slug that can go in a URL, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world".
Upper-case letters come back as lower case, so "Hello" becomes "hello".
A space between words becomes a dash, so "hello world" becomes "hello-world".
Several spaces in a row become one dash, so "hello   big world" (three spaces after "hello") becomes "hello-big-world".
Punctuation is removed from the slug, so "hello!" becomes "hello".
Letters outside a-z are removed rather than converted, so "héllo" becomes "hllo".

title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-safe slug

criteria.text: slugify turns a title into a slug that can be put in a URL, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world".
Upper-case letters in the title come out lower case, so "Hello" becomes "hello".

title: parseDuration is an unimplemented stub: it returns null for every input instead of seconds

criteria.text: A duration written as hours and minutes comes back as the total number of seconds, so parseDuration("1h30m") returns 5400.
A number followed by "s" is read as seconds, so parseDuration("45s") returns 45.
A number followed by "m" is read as minutes, so parseDuration("2m") returns 120.
A number followed by "h" is read as hours, so parseDuration("1h") returns 3600.
Hours, minutes and seconds together are added up, so parseDuration("1h30m15s") returns 5415.
A number with no unit is read as seconds, so parseDuration("90") returns 90.
A space between the parts is accepted, so parseDuration("1h 30m") returns 5400.
Unit letters can be upper case, so parseDuration("1H30M") returns 5400.
A part can be a decimal number, so parseDuration("1.5h") returns 5400.
